For example, when naming a mail domain, the user should satisfy both the
rules of this memo and those in RFC-822.  When creating a new host name,
the old rules for HOSTS.TXT should be followed.  This avoids problems
when old software is converted to use domain names.
requirements.required_behavior: The user should choose a name satisfying both this memo and RFC-822.
requirements.why_checkable: The recommendation refers to external RFC-822 naming rules that are not defined in this chunk; a complete implementation check cannot be derived here.

applications that use domain names (e.g., mail, TELNET).

<domain> ::= <subdomain> | " "

requirements.condition: When applying the preferred domain-name syntax recommended for compatibility with applications.

requirements.why_checkable: The mandatory initial letter and optional remainder establish a directly testable minimum label length of one.

requirements.quote:
The following syntax will result in fewer problems with many

applications that use domain names (e.g., mail, TELNET).

<domain> ::= <subdomain> | " "

<subdomain> ::= <label> | <subdomain> "." <label>

<label> ::= <letter> [ [ <ldh-str> ] <let-dig> ]

<ldh-str> ::= <let-dig-hyp> | <let-dig-hyp> <ldh-str>

<let-dig-hyp> ::= <let-dig> | "-"

<let-dig> ::= <letter> | <digit>

<letter> ::= any one of the 52 alphabetic characters A through Z in
upper case and a through z in lower case

<digit> ::= any one of the ten digits 0 through 9

Note that while upper and lower case letters are allowed in domain
names, no significance is attached to the case.  That is, two names with
the same spelling but different case are to be treated as if identical.

The labels must follow the rules for ARPANET host names.  They must
start with a letter, end with a letter or digit, and have as interior
characters only letters, digits, and hyphen.  There are also some
restrictions on the length.  Labels must be 63 characters or less.
requirements.condition: When applying the preferred domain-name syntax recommended for compatibility with applications.
requirements.required_behavior: Each label starts with a letter.
requirements.why_checkable: The first-character constraint can be checked in preferred-name validation or generation.
